title: MySQL/MariaDB outbound native client and msqlshim inbound server are opposite boundaries
summary: A future MySQL/MariaDB native outbound backend belongs in this backend family and will use the same capability/result/session contracts with exact target ABI handling for MYSQL_BIND. msqlshim is different: it is an inbound MySQL/MariaDB classic-wire compatibility server in front of NoSQLServer. The outbound client backend must not be coupled to msqlshim, and msqlshim must not absorb NoSQLServer source.
invariants: Outbound MySQL client integration and inbound MySQL wire impersonation solve opposite sides of the boundary.
The future outbound MySQL backend keeps its existing process/client route as fallback.
msqlshim owns classic MySQL/MariaDB wire/session compatibility; NoSQLServer owns SQL/storage semantics.
NoSQLServer remains package-reference-only from msqlshim; no embedded NoSQLServer.cls or vendor tree is permitted.
Native outbound MySQL work must satisfy the common backend capability/limitation publication contract.

provenance.claim: A future outbound MySQL/MariaDB native backend uses the same common contracts and retains an existing fallback.
msqlshim owns inbound MySQL/MariaDB classic wire/session compatibility and keeps NoSQLServer external by package reference.
